subject: Hospitality
title: Bar Design and Revenue Psychology
description: A fast breakdown of Bar Design and Revenue Psychology for builders.

hook.text: A well-designed bar earns $1,000+ per square meter annually. It's the most profitable space in most hotels per unit of area.

buildup.text: Back-bar displays—illuminated shelves of bottles—serve as both inventory and decoration.

discovery.text: Bar height (42 inches) and stool height (30 inches) are standardized for comfort and social interaction.

twist.text: Many hotels now place bars in lobby centers rather than separate rooms. Visibility increases impulse purchases from passing.

climax.text: Bar design blends function and theater: ice displays, dramatic lighting, signature cocktail presentations.

punchline.text: Highest revenue per square meter. The bar is the hotel's most profitable stage.

quiz.question: Why are hotel bars increasingly placed in lobby centers?
options: Visibility to passing guests increases impulse purchases
